title: Hard Bourbon Street jobs versus easier rooms and the West Coast
summary: Robinson contrasts the nonstop pressure of Bourbon Street joints with easier clubs, and describes crowded West Coast rooms.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Like, everybody could play a nice, slow, dreaming number. That's why, now you take, like, the dream, the dream room, now a man can play like he want over there. You play slow numbers, and play like you want them. You see? Then, if you play too many fast numbers, they flick them twice and say, no, see? Play some slow numbers. People want to dance. That's much like it, you see? I'll tell you. You take, when it used to be them tech dancers, you have around there, when they have the Budweiser and the Lovita. Them places wasn't hard as, like the paddock and like the famous door. Them, then, otherwise, piano could pick up a number, and either guitar, I mean, pick up a number, you see? And play the, the infant, infant rest. But now you, man, you gotta be, you gotta be blowing your brains all night. In the morning, next morning, when you go home, you ain't, you not, no service to yourself, or just go sleep and rest yourself. And like this time of year, if you ain't got some kind of a cool air conditioner, a good fan to keep cool, you'll burn up in working every night, too. You'll burn up. You'll never do feel good going on a job. When you go on them kind of jobs, you gotta work your spirit up, because you'll be tired when you're gone. But after you get there and get warm up, you'll come to yourself. But you don't, you don't feel good, then you know I done did it, I know. You don't feel good, man. You're lifting things, swole up and sleeping. You gotta play until you get your lips down flat. Down. Get the wife's bed, then you can go on back to wife. Every night you come there, you don't feel good. You don't, you don't feel like a man should feel. I know the way. Like I said, I don't mind playing a fella playing some man. But I wouldn't want none of that regular. No, no. And you take, and you take like, see we go on the west coast. We play the ten angels. We play at the, at the, at the Beverly Cabin. All in places. You see, when that place gets full of people, they tell you that the, the boss, you come tell us this. Come on, come on, get on, get on. Get on, go rush yourself. Hit about four or five more numbers. And they had, they had, they had a, they had a, they had a chain, had a chain by the, by the door. When they get some of the people that they couldn't, couldn't get no one. People be standing, standing by the door, gonna come on in. You see? Cause you can't sit to them tables like that.
